subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec allowlist matches, which command shapes may auto-execute when the authorization renderer cannot currently materialize an enforced command?
rationale: This is a security-boundary choice: fixing the production cron and approval-flood regression requires changing when matched commands bypass explicit approval, but raw shell execution could broaden what an allowlist entry authorizes.

options.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
options.body: Repair the planner/renderer for safe, enforceable cases such as plain argv and narrowly resolved home-prefixed paths, while preserving approval for dynamic shell expansion and wrapper payloads.

options.title: Document fail-closed limitation
options.body: Keep the current approval requirement and update the exec docs and warning text to explain that shell-shaped Darwin commands may not auto-execute.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell text
options.body: Run matched allowlist commands even without an enforced plan, accepting a larger shell-resolution trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable Darwin shapes
recommendation.body: Repair the planner/renderer for safe, enforceable cases such as plain argv and narrowly resolved home-prefixed paths, while preserving approval for dynamic shell expansion and wrapper payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant merged history for gateway exec approval regressions and durable trust is in Vincent Koc's approval-path work.
